one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-29. Q3 earnings are very likely outside it: CEG reported Q3 on Nov 7 2025, Nov 4 2024, Nov 6 2023 and Nov 8 2022, so Q3 2026 most likely lands in the first week of November. Inside the window: (1) PJM's one-time reliability backstop auction runs Sep 30 to Oct 21, but results are not published until Dec 2, and it targets new-build capacity, so it adds headline noise rather than a price event. (2) The FOMC decision on Oct 28, where prediction markets aggregated by DeFi Rate on Sep 30 show 43% hike and 57% hold (hike odds fell from about 66% a week earlier; volume not shown). Rising yields were one of the two named drivers of the September slide, so a hike is a modest negative for this long-duration name. (3) Calpine-seller supply: about 14M unlocked Calpine consideration shares may still be for sale after the June secondary. That is a known, slowly draining overhang. The stock has already bounced from $254.71 (Sep 18) to $264.58. There is no clear edge from reversal or momentum. I use a near-symmetric lognormal centred on about $265.5 (a tiny positive drift for mean reversion after a 13% supply-driven drop) with about 12.5% monthly sigma. That is a little below 47%/3.5 = 13.4%, because realized vol included the offering shock. Tails are slightly fattened.

fair_value.method: Blend of 12-month-forward P/E: 70% on the 2028 EPS the market will price in Sep 2027 ($15.0 x 19x = $285) and 30% on 2027 consensus EPS ($13.34 x 20x = $267). Blended value is about $280.

inputs_detail.derivation: 2027 consensus $13.34 grown about 12.5%. That haircuts management's >20% base-EPS CAGR to reflect 2026 guidance having missed consensus in March, and peer 2027 estimates being cut repeatedly (source 8). Management's full target would imply about $17.

CEG trades at about 21-23x forward today (source 5), versus Vistra at about 15-17x (source 9). CEG's implied forward multiple was about 30x at end-2025 ($366 on ~$12 2026 EPS, sources 1 and 10) and about 26x trailing at end-2024. The AI-power trade is de-rating across the IPP group (source 8), so I assume a further modest compression to 19x. That keeps a premium to VST for contracted nuclear.
Roughly today's 2027 multiple (about 21x per source 5), trimmed 1 turn toward the peer level (VST about 15x, source 9) to reflect a higher-rate backdrop (Fed hiking, source 11).

bear.story: The AI-power de-rating continues and Fed hikes lift yields further. The remaining 25M Calpine lock-up shares (released Jun 30 2027) add supply, and 2027 EPS is trimmed toward $12.5 on weaker merchant/ERCOT pricing or a Crane restart slip. The multiple compresses to a VST-like 15x: about $185.

base.story: 2026 lands in the $11.5-12.5 range and 2027 EPS is about $13.3-13.8. Buybacks absorb the Calpine overhang, Crane restart progresses toward 2027, and the multiple settles at about 19-20x forward. The stock recovers modestly toward $280, still well below the $349 mean target.

bull.story: New hyperscaler nuclear PPAs and PJM data-center rules favour existing nuclear, and the Crane restart comes early. EPS tracks management's >20% growth ($14.5 2027, about $17 2028), and the premium multiple partly returns (about 23x NTM), approaching the 2025 highs.

thesis_break_reason: $200 is about 15x 2027 consensus EPS, a VST-like multiple with no nuclear/contract premium. It is also about 12% below the 2026 low of $228.63, which came in the Calpine-offering and Citi-downgrade washout. A trade there would most likely mean the earnings path itself broke (guidance cut, a failed Crane restart, adverse PJM/FERC treatment of existing nuclear or colocation, or a hyperscaler pulling back on PPAs), rather than share-supply noise or rate volatility.

reasoning: Base rates first. CEG's own weekly history (Twelve Data) shows extreme regime swings: about $85 (end-2022) to $117 (end-2023) to $224 (end-2024) to $366 (end-2025), then a year stuck in a $229-334 range in 2026. 1-year realized vol is 47%, and 12-month moves of ±40% have been normal for this name, so a wide distribution is warranted. The 2026 drawdown matches the IPP group, not a CEG-specific break. VST is down 8% YTD and TLN 17% (as of mid-September), described as a 'valuation reset rather than an operational break' after the AI-power trade cooled. Fundamentals kept improving: Q2 adjusted EPS was $2.55 vs $2.33 consensus, 2026 guidance was raised to $11.50-12.50, 920 MW of new PPAs were signed, and Crane restart approvals arrived. At $264.58 the stock trades at about 22x 2026 and about 20x 2027 consensus ($13.34). That is down from about 30x forward at end-2025 but still above VST's 15-17x. The September slide (−13% in six sessions) was attributed to Calpine-seller share supply plus rising yields. I treat supply as a transient but recurring headwind (25M more shares unlock June 30 2027, inside the horizon). Macro base rates from prediction markets lean against a multiple rebound: the Fed hiked in September, October hike odds are 43% (DeFi Rate aggregate, Sep 30), there is an 86% chance of a 2026 hike, and Polymarket puts 35% on a recession by end-2027. On the other side, PJM capacity has cleared at the cap three straight times (the uncapped simulation was $555/MW-day), which keeps the structural nuclear value intact. Fair value from forward P/E is about $280, about 6% above spot. The ladder is a lognormal centred at about $274 (fair value plus drift, net of rate and supply headwinds) with about 42% annual sigma, slightly below realized 47% because some of that vol came from one-off offering shocks. The left tail is kept slightly fat for a guidance or policy break. Scenario mean (≈$281) is consistent. Analyst mean target $349 (22 analysts) is treated as an upper-bias anchor, not the answer; targets have been trimmed three quarters running. Research was limited to about 15 queries; some data sites (gurufocus, financecharts, predictionnews) blocked fetches, and prediction-market volumes were not visible on the aggregator page.
